================================================================================
  JAVASCRIPT PARSING AND COMPILATION — Complete Interview Reference
================================================================================

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. OVERVIEW: HOW BROWSERS EXECUTE JAVASCRIPT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  JavaScript is an interpreted language, but modern engines use
  Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation for performance.

  Pipeline:
    Source Code → Parsing → AST → Bytecode → Machine Code

  Key engines:
    V8         → Chrome, Edge, Node.js, Deno
    SpiderMonkey → Firefox
    JavaScriptCore (Nitro) → Safari, WebKit

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. DETAILED V8 PIPELINE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Stage 1: SCANNING / TOKENIZATION
    - Source code (UTF-8 text) → Stream of tokens
    - Tokens: keywords, identifiers, operators, literals, punctuation
    - Example: `let x = 5 + 3;`
      → [let] [x] [=] [5] [+] [3] [;]

  Stage 2: PARSING → AST
    - Tokens → Abstract Syntax Tree
    - AST = hierarchical tree representing code structure
    - Example AST for `let x = 5 + 3`:
        VariableDeclaration (kind: let)
          └── VariableDeclarator
                ├── Identifier (name: x)
                └── BinaryExpression (+)
                      ├── Literal (5)
                      └── Literal (3)

    Two parsing modes:
      Eager parsing:  Parse everything immediately (function bodies too)
      Lazy parsing:   Parse function bodies only when CALLED
                      (V8 uses this — skip parsing unused functions)

    Parser types in V8:
      Pre-parser: fast scan, determines scope, skips most of function body
      Full parser: complete parse, generates AST

  Stage 3: IGNITION (Bytecode Compiler)
    - AST → Bytecode (compact, register-based intermediate representation)
    - Bytecode is platform-independent (unlike machine code)
    - Executes on the Ignition interpreter
    - Fast to generate, lower peak memory than machine code
    - Collects type feedback (what types are passed to functions)

  Stage 4: TURBOFAN (Optimizing JIT Compiler)
    - Hot functions (called frequently) are identified
    - Using type feedback from Ignition: "this function always gets numbers"
    - Generates highly optimized machine code (SSA-based)
    - Inlines functions, eliminates dead code, vectorizes loops
    - Speculative optimization: assumes types stay consistent

  Stage 5: DEOPTIMIZATION (Bailout)
    - If type assumption is wrong: "function got a string, expected number"
    - V8 "deoptimizes" — discards machine code, reverts to bytecode
    - Called "bailout" or "deopt"
    - Multiple deoptimizations → V8 marks function "not optimizable"

  Full V8 Pipeline:
    Source → Tokenizer → Parser → AST
    → Ignition (bytecode) → Execute
    ↓ (hot function detected)
    → TurboFan (machine code) → Execute
    ↓ (type mismatch)
    → Deoptimize → Ignition bytecode

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. AST — ABSTRACT SYNTAX TREE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  The AST is the core representation that:
    - Transpilers (Babel) transform (AST → AST)
    - Bundlers (Webpack, Rollup) analyze
    - Linters (ESLint) check for issues
    - Minifiers (Terser) optimize

  AST Tools:
    astexplorer.net — interactive AST explorer for any language
    @babel/parser  — Babel's JS parser
    acorn, espree  — popular parsers used by ESLint, Webpack

  Why AST matters:
    Tree shaking: bundlers analyze AST import/export statements
    Code splitting: find dynamic import() boundaries
    Dead code elimination: detect unreachable code

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. COMPILATION STRATEGIES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  AOT (Ahead-of-Time) Compilation:
    - Compiles BEFORE execution (like C/C++)
    - Faster startup (no compilation overhead at runtime)
    - Native app performance
    - Example: Dart→native (Flutter), AssemblyScript, Emscripten

  JIT (Just-in-Time) Compilation:
    - Compiles DURING execution when needed
    - V8, SpiderMonkey use JIT
    - Advantages: adapts to actual data (type-specialized code)
    - Disadvantages: startup overhead, potential deoptimization

  Interpreted:
    - No compilation; bytecodes executed by interpreter
    - Ignition in V8 interprets bytecode
    - Faster startup for small scripts (no compilation overhead)

  Hybrid (modern browsers):
    - Initially interpret bytecode (fast startup)
    - Hot paths JIT-compiled (high throughput)
    - Best of both worlds

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. JIT OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  5.1 INLINE CACHING (IC)
    Problem: Property access like obj.foo requires hash lookup every time
    Solution: IC caches the property's memory offset after first access
    Monomorphic IC: single type → fastest
    Polymorphic IC: few types → slower
    Megamorphic IC: many types → no caching, slowest

    Code example:
    function add(obj) { return obj.x + obj.y; }
    add({x:1, y:2})  // IC caches layout of {x,y}
    add({x:3, y:4})  // IC hit — fast
    add({x:1, y:2, z:3})  // different hidden class → IC miss

  5.2 HIDDEN CLASSES (Shapes/Maps)
    Problem: JS objects are dynamic (properties can be added/removed anytime)
    Solution: V8 assigns each unique object "shape" a "hidden class"
    Objects with the same properties in the same order share a hidden class

    Performance tip — consistent object shape:
    // Good: same shape
    function Point(x, y) { this.x = x; this.y = y; }
    const p1 = new Point(1, 2);  // hidden class A
    const p2 = new Point(3, 4);  // same hidden class A → IC hit

    // Bad: different shapes
    const p1 = { x: 1, y: 2 };
    const p2 = { y: 2, x: 1 };  // DIFFERENT hidden class (property order matters!)

    Property addition order matters:
    const obj = {};
    obj.x = 1; obj.y = 2; // shape: {x,y}
    const obj2 = {};
    obj2.y = 1; obj2.x = 2; // different shape: {y,x}

  5.3 FUNCTION INLINING
    Small functions called frequently are inlined (code copied to call site)
    Eliminates function call overhead and enables further optimization

  5.4 ESCAPE ANALYSIS
    If an object doesn't "escape" a function, V8 can allocate it on the
    stack (fast) instead of the heap (requires GC)

  5.5 DEAD CODE ELIMINATION
    Code paths that are never reached are removed during optimization

  5.6 LOOP OPTIMIZATION
    Loop unrolling, vectorization (SIMD), strength reduction

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. HOW JAVASCRIPT IS LOADED
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  <script> execution timing:

  Regular <script>:
    HTML: ─────⛔ JS Download ─⛔ JS Execute ──────────
    Parse:     BLOCKED     |              RESUMES

  <script async>:
    HTML: ─────────────────────────────────────────
    JS:        ─── Download ──⛔ Execute
    (executes as soon as downloaded, may interrupt parsing)

  <script defer>:
    HTML: ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    JS:        ─── Download ────────────────────── Execute (after parse)

  <script type="module">:
    - Deferred behavior by default
    - Strict mode
    - Own lexical scope
    - Supports static import/export
    - Supports dynamic import()

  Script execution order guarantees:
    Regular: in order
    async: no order guarantee
    defer: maintains source order
    modules: defer order

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. V8 MEMORY: HEAP AND GARBAGE COLLECTION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Heap Spaces:
    New Space (Young Generation):
      - Small (~1-8MB), contains newly created objects
      - Collected frequently (Scavenger/Minor GC)
      - Most objects die young (generational hypothesis)

    Old Space (Old Generation):
      - Objects surviving 2+ minor GCs promoted here
      - Collected less frequently (Major GC / Mark-Sweep-Compact)
      - Larger (up to several GB)

    Code Space:
      - JIT-compiled machine code lives here
      - Executable memory

    Large Object Space:
      - Objects larger than 256KB (bypass new space)

  Garbage Collection Algorithms:
    Scavenger (Minor GC — Young Gen):
      - Cheney's algorithm (semi-space copying)
      - From-space → To-space (live objects copied, dead reclaimed)
      - Very fast but limited to new space

    Mark-Sweep-Compact (Major GC — Old Gen):
      - Mark: trace live objects from roots (global, stack)
      - Sweep: reclaim memory of unmarked objects
      - Compact (optional): move live objects together (defragmentation)
      - Slower (entire heap traversal)

    Incremental Marking:
      - Break marking into small increments
      - Interleave with JS execution → less jank from GC pauses

    Concurrent Marking (V8):
      - Marking done on background thread (concurrent with JS)
      - Even less impact on frame timing

  GC Triggers:
    - New space fills up → Scavenger
    - Old space fills up → Major GC
    - Time-based heuristics

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
8. WRITING JIT-FRIENDLY CODE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  8.1 Use consistent types:
    function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
    add(1, 2);    // always numbers → monomorphic → JIT optimized
    add("a","b"); // now string too → becomes polymorphic → slower

  8.2 Don't change object shapes after creation:
    // Good
    const obj = { x: 0, y: 0 };  // Create with all properties
    obj.x = 10;  // OK

    // Bad
    const obj = {};
    if (condition) obj.x = 10;  // Different shapes
    obj.y = 20;                 // depending on condition

  8.3 Use class-based objects (stable hidden classes):
    class Point {
      constructor(x, y) { this.x = x; this.y = y; }
    }

  8.4 Avoid delete operator:
    delete obj.prop; // changes hidden class → deoptimizes
    // Instead: set to null/undefined

  8.5 Use typed arrays for numeric data:
    new Int32Array(1000)   // Contiguous, typed memory → no boxing
    new Float64Array(1000) // vs regular Array with numbers (boxed)

  8.6 Avoid try/catch in hot paths:
    V8 historically couldn't optimize functions with try/catch
    (less of an issue in modern V8, but still consider)

  8.7 Avoid arguments object:
    function f() { return arguments[0]; } // slower
    function f(x) { return x; }           // faster, x directly in register

  8.8 Short functions inline better:
    Keep hot functions small so V8 can inline them at call sites

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
9. SOURCE MAPS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Problem: Minified/transpiled code is unreadable for debugging
  Solution: Source maps — JSON files mapping minified code back to original

  Structure:
    {
      "version": 3,
      "file": "app.min.js",
      "sources": ["app.ts", "utils.ts"],
      "mappings": "AAAA,SAAS..."  // VLQ-encoded position mappings
    }

  Comment in minified file:
    //# sourceMappingURL=app.min.js.map

  Inline source map:
    //# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64,...

  Tools:
    Webpack, Rollup, Vite, esbuild, TypeScript — all generate source maps
    Chrome DevTools automatically applies source maps when available

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
10. WEBASSEMBLY (WASM)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  What is WebAssembly?
    - Binary instruction format for a virtual stack machine
    - Runs in browser with near-native performance
    - Compiled from C, C++, Rust, Go, etc.
    - NOT a replacement for JavaScript — a complement

  Characteristics:
    • Binary format → small, fast to decode
    • Sandboxed (same security model as JS)
    • Language-agnostic (C++ → WASM → browser)
    • No DOM access directly (must call JS interop)
    • Linear memory model
    • Deterministic (no garbage collection issues)
    • Threads via SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics

  Use cases:
    • Video/image processing (codecs, filters)
    • Game engines (Unity, Unreal → WASM)
    • CAD applications
    • Scientific computation
    • FFmpeg in browser

  JS ↔ WASM Interop:
    const module = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch('app.wasm'));
    const result = module.instance.exports.add(1, 2);

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
11. INTERVIEW QUESTIONS & ANSWERS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Q: How does V8 execute JavaScript?
A: Source → Tokenizer → AST via Parser → Ignition compiles to bytecode
   → Bytecode interpreted. Hot functions → TurboFan JIT-compiles to
   optimized machine code. If type assumptions are wrong → deoptimizes
   back to bytecode.

Q: What is JIT compilation?
A: Just-in-Time compilation compiles code during execution based on
   runtime observations (type feedback). V8's Ignition collects type
   info, TurboFan generates optimized machine code for hot paths.
   Unlike AOT (ahead-of-time), JIT can adapt to actual data patterns.

Q: What are hidden classes in V8?
A: V8 assigns objects a "hidden class" (shape) based on their structure
   (properties and their order). Objects with the same shape share a
   hidden class, enabling efficient property access via inline caches.
   Changing object structure (adding properties dynamically, delete)
   creates new hidden classes, causing IC misses and deoptimization.

Q: What is inline caching?
A: A JIT optimization where the offset of an object property is cached
   after first access. Subsequent accesses to the same property on
   objects of the same hidden class use the cached offset (no hash
   lookup). Monomorphic (one type) is fastest; megamorphic (many types) bypasses IC.

Q: What is deoptimization in V8?
A: When TurboFan's type assumptions are violated (e.g., function always
   got numbers, then got a string), V8 discards the compiled machine code
   and falls back to Ignition bytecode. Repeated deoptimizations mark
   a function as non-optimizable.

Q: What is the difference between async and defer?
A: Both download scripts without blocking HTML parsing.
   async: executes as soon as downloaded (unordered, may interrupt parsing).
   defer: executes after HTML fully parsed, in source order, before DOMContentLoaded.
   Use defer for app scripts needing DOM; async for independent third-party scripts.

Q: What is lazy parsing in V8?
A: V8 uses lazy parsing (pre-parsing) to avoid fully parsing function bodies
   until they're called. The pre-parser scans quickly to determine scopes
   without building a full AST. Reduces startup time for large bundles with
   many unused functions.

Q: What is WebAssembly and when would you use it?
A: WASM is a binary instruction format that runs in browsers at near-native
   speed. Compiled from C/C++/Rust. Used for performance-critical tasks:
   video encoding, game engines, CAD, scientific computing. Complements
   JS (doesn't replace it) — WASM modules called from JS.

Q: How can you write JavaScript that V8 can optimize well?
A: Use consistent types in functions, don't change object shapes after
   creation, avoid delete operator, use class-based objects for stable
   hidden classes, use typed arrays for numeric data, avoid polymorphic
   function arguments.

================================================================================
  KEY TAKEAWAYS
================================================================================
  • V8 pipeline: Source → AST → Ignition (bytecode) → TurboFan (machine code)
  • JIT: interprets first, compiles hot paths, deoptimizes on type violations
  • Hidden classes: V8's shape-based optimization; keep object shapes stable
  • Inline caching: caches property offsets; monomorphic = fastest
  • async: download parallel, execute immediately (unordered)
  • defer: download parallel, execute after parse (ordered, before DCL)
  • Write JIT-friendly code: consistent types, stable shapes, typed arrays
  • WebAssembly: near-native performance for compute-heavy tasks
================================================================================
